The ''' 1944 [[German football championship]]''', the 37th edition of the competition, was won by [[Dresdner SC]], the club defending its 1943 title by defeating ''[[Luftwaffe]]'' team [[LSV Hamburg]] in the final.<ref>[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duitchamp.html (West) Germany -List of champions] rsssf.org, accessed: 22 December 2015</ref><ref>[http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/dresdner-sc/1/ Dresdner SC » Steckbrief] {{in lang|de}} Weltfussball.de – Dresdner SC honours, accessed: 22 December 2015</ref>

The final years of the German Championship during the war saw many military teams compete in the championship, ''Luftwaffe'' teams, ''Luftwaffensportvereine'', short ''LSV'', and, ''[[Wehrmacht]]'' teams, ''Wehrmachtssportvereine'', short ''WSV'', became very competitive.<ref>[http://www.augsburger-allgemeine.de/sport/Als-Wien-deutscher-Meister-wurde-id31162997.html Als Wien deutscher Meister wurde] {{in lang|de}} ''[[Augsburger Allgemeine]]'' – When Vienna became German champions, published: 3 September 2015, accessed: 26 December 2015</ref>

Dresden's [[Helmut Schön]], who would later coach Germany to the [[1974 FIFA World Cup]], became the top scorer of the 1944 championship with 14 goals, the second-highest individual amount of any player in the history of the competition from 1903 to 1963.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/deutsche-meisterschaft/ |title=Deutsche Meisterschaft » Torschützenkönige |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 2 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=German championship: Top goal scorer}}</ref>

It was the last edition of the tournament during the [[Second World War]], with the competition not being held again until [[1948 German football championship|1948]]. The thirty-one [[1943–44 Gauliga|1943–44]] [[Gauliga]] champions, two more than in the previous season,<ref>''kicker Allmanach 1990'', page: 243-245</ref> competed in a single-leg knock out competition to determine the national champion.<ref name="Rsssf" >[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duithistpre45.html German championship 1944] rsssf.org, accessed: 25 December 2015</ref>

Dresdner SC became the last club to be awarded the ''[[Viktoria (trophy)|Viktoria]]'', the annual trophy for the German champions from 1903 to 1944. The trophy disappeared during the final stages of the war, did not resurface until after the [[German reunification]] and was put on display at the DFB headquarters in [[Frankfurt]] until 2015, when it was moved to the new ''[[Deutsches Fußballmuseum]]'' in [[Dortmund]].<ref>[https://www.dfb.de/news/detail/pokale-auf-reisen-viktoria-und-co-wandern-ins-fussballmuseum-123277/ POKALE AUF REISEN: VIKTORIA UND CO. WANDERN INS FUSSBALLMUSEUM] {{in lang|de}} DFB website, accessed: 27 December 2015</ref>
